crm.label: Sales pipeline
crm.description: A fictitious B2B hardware vendor's 2017 pipeline, published by Maven Analytics as a teaching dataset. Used for pipeline shape only. No finding from this domain describes a real market, and it must never be compared to the acquisition domain as though the two were one business.

acquisition.label: Client acquisition and revenue
acquisition.description: Real marketing-qualified leads, signed clients, and the orders those clients went on to fulfil, from Olist, a Brazilian marketplace, between June 2017 and November 2018.

opportunities.description: Every opportunity, open or closed. deal_stage is one of Prospecting, Engaging, Won, Lost.
caveats: close_value is 0 for Lost deals and NULL for open ones. These mean different things and must not be collapsed.
1,425 opportunities name no account. Any account-level metric must exclude them explicitly.
Every Prospecting opportunity lacks an engage_date, so cycle time is undefined for them by construction.

accounts.description: The client companies opportunities are opened against.

products.description: Product catalogue with list prices, grouped into series.

sales_teams.description: Agents, the manager they report to, and their regional office.

leads.description: Leads that passed marketing qualification, with the channel and landing page that produced them.
caveats: origin 'unknown' is a recorded value meaning the source could not be identified. origin 'not_recorded' is this pipeline's label for a NULL. They are different facts and must not be merged.

deals.description: Leads that converted into signed clients, joined to the revenue that client generated in the 90 days after signing.
caveats: window_complete marks deals that had a full 90-day observation window. Every rate over this table must filter on it. The commerce data ends 2018-09-03 while deals close through 2018-11-14, so deals signed late cannot show revenue by construction, not by failure.
revenue_90d is 0 for clients that never billed. That is a real outcome, not a missing value.

seller_performance.grain: One row per selling client, lifetime.
seller_performance.description: Lifetime orders, revenue, and average review score per client, excluding cancelled orders.

orders.description: Orders with status and the full set of delivery timestamps.
caveats: Cancelled orders are present. Every revenue metric excludes them.
2,965 orders have no delivery timestamp. Delivery metrics exclude them.

order_items.grain: One row per item line within an order.
order_items.description: Item lines with price and freight.
caveats: One row per line, not per order. Any per-order metric must aggregate first or it will double count.

customers.grain: One row per customer record on an order.
customers.description: End customers, with city and state.
caveats: customer_id identifies an order's customer record, not a person. customer_unique_id identifies the person across orders. Counting customers by customer_id overstates the customer base by 3,345.

reviews.description: Review scores from 1 to 5 with timestamps.
caveats: review_id is not unique; one review can attach to more than one order.

manager.description: The manager an agent reports to.

channel.description: Acquisition channel of a lead. Values include organic_search, paid_search, social, unknown, direct_traffic, email, referral, display, other, other_publicities, not_recorded.

business_segment.description: The market segment a signed client sells into.

lead_type.description: Size and channel classification of the lead at qualification.

customer_state.description: Two-letter Brazilian state of the end customer.

order_status.description: delivered, shipped, canceled, unavailable, and others.

opportunity_count.description: Number of opportunities, open or closed.

win_rate.sql: AVG(CASE WHEN crm_opportunities.is_won THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END)
win_rate.description: Share of closed opportunities that were won. Open deals are excluded because their outcome is not yet known; including them understates the rate by treating "undecided" as "lost".
win_rate.reporting_note: Quote with a confidence interval whenever it is compared across groups. Differences between sectors in this data are inside sampling noise.

booked_value.sql: SUM(CASE WHEN crm_opportunities.is_won THEN crm_opportunities.close_value ELSE 0 END)
booked_value.description: Total value of won deals. Lost and open deals contribute nothing.

avg_won_value.sql: AVG(CASE WHEN crm_opportunities.is_won THEN crm_opportunities.close_value END)
avg_won_value.description: Mean value of won deals. The CASE returns NULL rather than 0 for non-wins so that AVG skips them; using 0 would drag the mean toward zero.

median_cycle_days.description: Median days from engagement to close. Median rather than mean: the distribution is bimodal and a mean describes no real deal.

conversion_rate.description: Share of qualified leads that signed. Measured over every lead, because nothing about a lead becoming a deal is censored.

attachment_rate.sql: AVG(CASE WHEN deal_outcomes.ever_sold THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END)
attachment_rate.description: Share of signed clients that generated any revenue. The filter on window_complete is mandatory: without it the figure is 45.0% instead of 51.4%, and the difference is entirely an artefact of when the data ends.

revenue_90d.description: Revenue billed by signed clients in their first 90 days.

median_days_to_close.description: Median days from first marketing contact to signature.

order_revenue.description: Item revenue on live orders. Excludes freight, which is a pass-through cost rather than seller revenue, and excludes cancelled orders.

order_count.description: Distinct orders. Always COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) when order_items is in the query, or an order with three lines counts three times.

on_time_delivery_rate.sql:
AVG(CASE WHEN orders.order_delivered_customer_date
              <= orders.order_estimated_delivery_date
         THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END)
on_time_delivery_rate.description: Share of delivered orders that arrived on or before the estimate. Undelivered orders are excluded rather than counted as late.

avg_delivery_days.description: Mean days from purchase to delivery.

joins.note: Excludes the 1,425 opportunities with no account. Use a LEFT JOIN only if the question is about opportunities regardless of account.
Only 380 of 842 signed clients appear here; the rest never listed.

forbidden_joins.reason: The CRM pipeline is a synthetic dataset about a fictitious hardware vendor. The acquisition funnel is real data from a Brazilian marketplace. They share no entity, no market, and no time period. Joining them produces a number that describes nothing.
Same as above - different businesses entirely.
Same as above - different businesses entirely.
Customers are end consumers buying from the marketplace. Leads are businesses being recruited to sell on it. They are opposite sides of the market and share no key.

refusals.response: Neither dataset records cost. Revenue is available, but profit, margin, customer acquisition cost, and return on investment cannot be computed from anything here. Answering would require cost data the business holds elsewhere.

The sales pipeline and the acquisition funnel are separate datasets from separate businesses, one of them synthetic. A figure spanning both would be meaningless, so the layer refuses rather than computing it.
refusals.does_not_apply_when: The question can be answered inside one domain. Resolve the domain from the vocabulary before considering this rule. Win rate, deal stage, opportunity, sales agent, manager, regional office, product series, list price, close value and sector are CRM terms and are answerable from the CRM domain alone - "client" in that context means an account. Lead, channel, marketing-qualified, signed client, attachment, business segment, order, seller, review and delivery are acquisition terms. Only refuse when answering would require joining the two, or when the question explicitly asks to compare them.

refusals.response: This is observational data with no experiment and no control group. It can show that two things moved together; it cannot show that one caused the other. The honest answer is the association, labelled as such.
The layer reports what happened in the observed window. It has no model for what happens next, and the data ends in 2018, so any forecast would be invented rather than estimated.
Customers and sales representatives are anonymised at source - the data carries hashed identifiers only. No individual can be identified, and the layer will not attempt to.
The sales pipeline covers 2017 and the acquisition data runs from June 2017 to November 2018. Any question about a period outside that has no data behind it.
That asks about something the layer does not define. Rather than guess at a column that might mean it, the layer declines and names what it does cover.

forbid: transaction and session control (BEGIN, COMMIT, SET, PRAGMA)
file and extension access (COPY, INSTALL, LOAD, read_csv, read_json)
subqueries in more than three levels of nesting
